root_cause.text: Airoha QDMA RX error handling in `airoha_qdma_rx_process()` only returned the page_pool fragment when no partial skb existed, so fragments from the non-linear skb path could be dropped on error before being attached to the skb and never recycled back to the page pool, causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `else` guard and unconditionally calls `page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true);` in the RX error path, and the CVE description states that “the page_pool fragment will not be linked to the skb so it will not return to the pool in the airoha_qdma_rx_process() error path.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes the `else` guard and unconditionally calls `page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true);` in the RX error path, and the CVE description states that “the page_pool fragment will not be linked to the skb so it will not return to the pool in the airoha_qdma_rx_process() error path.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Always return the RX page to the page pool after handling the buffer to fix a missing page release in the receive path.
intent_record.what: In `airoha_qdma_rx_process()`, the `page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true);` call was moved out of the `else` branch and is now executed unconditionally after the `if (q->skb)` block.
intent_record.how: After processing an RX descriptor, the page is now returned to the page pool regardless of whether an skb was present and freed. This removes the previous path where pages associated with an skb would not be released here, preventing a potential page leak or resource retention in the RX completion path.

grouping_result.intent: Always return the RX page to the page pool after handling the buffer to fix a missing page release in the receive path.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly fixes missing RX page release by always returning the page to the page pool, which matches the reported leak in QDMA RX error handling where non-linear skb fragments were not recycled.

candidates.rationale: This conditional makes page recycling depend on whether a partial skb already exists. In the vulnerable path, pages used for non-linear skb fragments could be skipped when q->skb was present, leading to leaked RX pages instead of always returning them to the page pool.
This branch only frees the partial skb and does not ensure the current RX page is returned to the page pool, which is the missing release causing the leak on error handling.
Clearing the skb pointer ends the partial-skb state without releasing the associated RX page, contributing to the failure to recycle fragments back to the page pool.
This else branch shows the only path where page_pool_put_full_page() was called, meaning pages in the q->skb path were not recycled and could be leaked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional split the RX error handling into a partial-skb path and a no-skb path. Because the page_pool return was only done in the else branch, fragments associated with an existing q->skb could bypass recycling and leak.
In the partial-skb error path, this only freed the skb object and did not return the RX page to the page pool, which is the missing recycle operation described in the root cause.
Clearing the skb pointer here ended the partial-skb state without ensuring the associated fragment page was recycled, allowing the page to be dropped on error.
This branch structure shows that page_pool_put_full_page() was only reachable when q->skb was absent, leaving the q->skb path without page release and causing the leak.

Author: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>

    net: airoha: Fix page recycling in airoha_qdma_rx_process()
    
    Do not recycle the page twice in airoha_qdma_rx_process routine in case
    of error. Just run dev_kfree_skb() if the skb has been allocated and marked

    been allocated yet.

Before the fix, it unconditionally did `page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true); dev_kfree_skb(q->skb); q->skb = NULL;`, which could recycle the page even when `q->skb` had already been allocated and was still using the fragment, matching the root cause of improper page recycling / leak handling on error. In this commit, the code now distinguishes the cases: `if (q->skb) { dev_kfree_skb(q->skb); q->skb = NULL; } else { page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true); }`, which is the described fix. The earlier checks also show the error path is reached when `!len || data_len < len`, so the function body is sufficient to determine both the presence of the bug in the pre-fix logic and that this version already contains the fix.
